cio.executive_summary: BMO presents a more nuanced picture than its Big 6 peers. The Bank of the West acquisition has been slower and more costly to integrate than management guided, and US loan losses are running above peer averages. The Canadian franchise is solid, and the 4.7% dividend yield provides income while waiting. At 1.5x book value, BMO is not cheap enough to be a conviction buy nor is there a compelling reason to sell a high-quality Canadian bank. Hold and monitor Q1 2026 earnings for signs of US credit quality stabilization.
cio.key_disagreements_addressed: The most significant disagreement was between the bear advocate (Sell, $112 target) and the bull advocate (Buy, $148 target) — a $36 spread on a $127 stock. The bear's concern about US PCL trends is the most important variable to watch. I chose HOLD over BUY because the risk advisor's point about the 1.3:1 risk/reward ratio being below threshold is compelling. A HOLD is appropriate when the evidence is genuinely mixed.
cio.account_specific_note: For Alex's RRSP, BMO should remain a HOLD at current sizing. Do not add to the position before Q1 2026 earnings. If US PCL ratios improve, upgrade to Buy. If US PCL ratios worsen again, the bear case gains credibility and a trim would be warranted.
